what: Per-person features -- what a name is said to mean, the titles the texts give, and the other names they give -- published ONLY where this archive's own tier-1 corpus carries the value as whole words within three lines of the person's own name, and citing THAT line. Tolkien Gateway is recorded as the finding aid that led here and is never the authority.
ruling: C831, 2 September 2026: a Tolkien Gateway datum may reach a reader only where TG itself cites a Tolkien text, and what the archive carries is THAT cite -- Tolkien's, not TG's. The split is per claim, never per article (C499).
how: Every locus here is MINTED by this module against the corpus, by the word reader ardatext.words_of, and never taken from the proposal: the proposal's loci are minted by ardatext.verify, which returns the first SUBSTRING hit, and 140 of its 667 strongest candidates point at a line where the value does not stand as a word. ardatext.verify_at is run on every published locus and its verdict is recorded per item whether it agrees or not -- it anchors on the same first substring hit, so a disagreement here is a fact about that instrument and not about the line.

feature_labels.etymology: what the name is said to mean
feature_labels.other_names: the other names the texts give

held_because.not_machine_confirmable: the proposal stamps this feature `machine_confirmable: false`. Its values are common English adjectives -- Golden, Blue, Short, Brown -- and the workbench's first pass graded 134 of 144 characteristics rows [C] on a co-occurrence match, including Elendil's height on the word 'Over'. A word that stands everywhere confirms nothing, and no instrument in this archive can confirm these. They need a human reading the cited passage.
held_because.not_attestable: a pronunciation respelling is not a thing a corpus can attest. TG's |pronun= is Appendix E applied by hand by wiki editors and 173 of its 174 values across the whole wiki carry no citation of any kind.
held_because.not_distinctive: the value is a common word, a field label, or a fragment of the person's own name, so a corpus match on it would confirm the vocabulary and not the claim.
held_because.corpus_silent: no tier-1 corpus file holds this value as whole words. C831 lets a reader see a TG datum only where a Tolkien text carries it; this archive's Tolkien texts do not.
held_because.not_beside_the_person: the value stands in this archive's tier-1 corpus and so does the person's name, and no ONE LINE carries both in a form that attributes the value to this person. Four things put an item here and they are all about the LOCUS, never about the claim: the two never share a line; every mention of the name on that line is a genitive (`the Heir of Isildur was crowned King of Gondor` -- a true claim on a line about Aragorn); another person the archive holds stands between them (`Isildur had established Meneldil as King of Gondor`); or the two match the line under folding but not as a token sequence, so the archive cannot say precisely where they stand. The claim may well be true. This module has no line it can show a reader for it, and a citation a reader cannot check is what rule 1 forbids.
held_because.source_grants_no_marker: the file the value was minted in is not granted [C] by site/arda_sources.json -- it is not a primary text of content tier 1 or 2 -- so the attestation is someone else's book about Tolkien rather than Tolkien.
held_because.value_is_a_book_title: the value is the title of a book on this archive's own shelf, taken from the one table in map/cited_check.py that says how the archive names its books. TG carries `The Lord of the Rings` in person/sauron's titles, and every corpus line that could support it is a sentence about the book. A book and a character genuinely stand together on such a line and no co-occurrence rule can separate them, so this is refused by what the value IS.
held_because.not_set_as_a_name: a title or a by-name is a proper noun and the texts set it as one -- `the Necromancer`, `Prince of Dol Amroth`, `Annatar`. No content word of this value stands CAPITALISED in the line that carries it, so the line uses the words and does not name anybody with them: `the shadow of Mordor reached` is not a naming of Sauron, though `The Shadow` is a true by-name of his. The claim may be right; this line is not evidence of it. Not applied to name-meanings, which are not proper nouns and never were.
held_because.no_published_route: the archive holds no published person/<id>.html for this person, so there is no reader to reach. Measured with `git -C site ls-files person`, never with a glob of the disk.
held_because.tg_cites_a_book_not_a_passage: TG's only support is a bibliographic reference to a Tolkien book -- C831 permits it in principle, and this module declines it: a reference the archive cannot open is not a locus a reader can check, and rule 1 is not satisfied by naming a book. Held, counted, and put to the owner rather than published quietly.
held_because.tg_cites_nothing: TG cites nothing at all for this datum. C831: the other 55.5% is extracted, tiered, searchable by the archive and invisible to readers.

held_crosscut.what: The SAME held items, seen a second way: what Tolkien Gateway offered as support for the row each came from. This is not a class list and does not add to `held` -- it re-partitions it, and its denominator is held_total.
